questions.question: A horizontal piston–cylinder contains gas at pressure $P_0$. The piston has area $A = 50\ \mathrm{cm^2}$ and mass $m = 0$. Atmospheric pressure is $P_{\mathrm{atm}} = 1.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$. What is the equilibrium gas pressure?
questions.answer:
For a horizontal frictionless piston with no mass and no applied force, the gas pressure equals atmospheric pressure:

$P_{\text{gas}} = P_{\text{atm}} = 1.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$

At equilibrium, the net force on the piston is zero: $P_{\text{gas}} \cdot A = P_{\text{atm}} \cdot A$

questions.question: A vertical cylinder with a frictionless piston (mass $m = 2\ \mathrm{kg}$, area $A = 0.01\ \mathrm{m^2}$) sits with the piston on top. Atmospheric pressure is $P_0 = 1.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$, $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. Find the gas pressure inside the cylinder.
questions.answer:
Force balance on the piston (upward = downward):

$P_{\text{gas}} \cdot A = P_0 \cdot A + mg$

$P_{\text{gas}} = P_0 + \dfrac{mg}{A} = 1.0\times10^5 + \dfrac{2 \times 10}{0.01}$

$= 1.0\times10^5 + 2000 = 1.02\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$

questions.question: A piston–cylinder has gas at $T_1 = 300\ \mathrm{K}$. The piston (area $A = 0.02\ \mathrm{m^2}$, mass $m = 4\ \mathrm{kg}$) is in equilibrium. $P_0 = 1.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$, $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, initial length $L_1 = 0.5\ \mathrm{m}$. The gas is heated to $T_2 = 450\ \mathrm{K}$. Find the new length $L_2$.
questions.answer:
Pressure is constant (isobaric) since the piston weight and atmosphere don't change:

$P = P_0 + mg/A = 1.0\times10^5 + 4\times10/0.02 = 1.0\times10^5 + 2000 \approx 1.02\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$

Isobaric: $V \propto T \Rightarrow L \propto T$ (same cross-section):

$L_2 = L_1 \times \dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = 0.5 \times \dfrac{450}{300} = 0.75\ \mathrm{m}$

questions.question: A cylinder with a fixed piston (rigid, locked) contains gas at $P_1 = 1.5\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ and $T_1 = 300\ \mathrm{K}$. The gas is heated to $T_2 = 450\ \mathrm{K}$. Find $P_2$. Then the piston is released and expands isobarically to $T_3 = 600\ \mathrm{K}$. Find $V_3/V_1$.
questions.answer:
**Heating with locked piston (isochoric):**

$P_2 = P_1 \cdot \dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = 1.5\times10^5 \times \dfrac{450}{300} = 2.25\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$

**Isobaric expansion from state 2 to 3** (at $P_2 = $ const):

$\dfrac{V_3}{V_2} = \dfrac{T_3}{T_2} = \dfrac{600}{450} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

Since $V_1 = V_2$ (locked piston during step 1):

$\dfrac{V_3}{V_1} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

questions.question: A vertical cylinder has a piston of mass $m = 5\ \mathrm{kg}$ and cross-sectional area $A = 100\ \mathrm{cm^2} = 0.01\ \mathrm{m^2}$. A block of mass $M = 10\ \mathrm{kg}$ is placed on the piston. Find: (a) the initial gas pressure (without block), (b) the new pressure (with block), (c) the fractional change in volume if $T$ stays constant.
questions.answer:
$P_0 = 1.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$, $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$

**(a)** Without block: $P_1 = P_0 + mg/A = 1.0\times10^5 + 5\times10/0.01 = 1.05\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$

**(b)** With block: $P_2 = P_0 + (m+M)g/A = 1.0\times10^5 + 15\times10/0.01 = 1.15\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$

**(c)** Isothermal: $P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2$

$\dfrac{V_2}{V_1} = \dfrac{P_1}{P_2} = \dfrac{1.05}{1.15} \approx 0.913$

Volume decreases by about $8.7\%$.

questions.question: A piston–cylinder with piston area $A$ is initially in equilibrium at $P = P_0 + mg/A$ (piston mass $m$, atmospheric pressure $P_0$). The gas occupies length $L$. A weight $F$ is slowly placed on the piston. Write the new equilibrium pressure and the new length (isothermal).
questions.answer:
**New pressure** (force balance with additional load $F$):

$P_\text{new} = P_0 + \dfrac{mg + F}{A}$

**New length** (isothermal: $PV = $ const, with $V = AL$):

$P_\text{old} \cdot AL = P_\text{new} \cdot AL_\text{new}$

$L_\text{new} = L \cdot \dfrac{P_\text{old}}{P_\text{new}} = L \cdot \dfrac{P_0 A + mg}{P_0 A + mg + F}$

The new length is shorter since $P_\text{new} > P_\text{old}$.

questions.question: A piston–cylinder contains $n = 0.1\ \mathrm{mol}$ of monatomic ideal gas at $T = 300\ \mathrm{K}$ and pressure $P = 2.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ (set by the piston equilibrium). The gas is heated at constant pressure until $T' = 600\ \mathrm{K}$. Find: (a) the work done by the gas, (b) $\Delta U$, (c) the heat input.
questions.answer:
**(a)** Isobaric work: $W = nR\Delta T = 0.1 \times 8.31 \times 300 = 249.3\ \mathrm{J}$

**(b)** $\Delta U = \dfrac{3}{2}nR\Delta T = \dfrac{3}{2} \times 249.3 = 373.95\ \mathrm{J}$

**(c)** $Q = \Delta U + W = 373.95 + 249.3 = 623.25\ \mathrm{J}$

(Or: $Q = nC_P\Delta T = 0.1 \times \frac{5}{2} \times 8.31 \times 300 = 623.25\ \mathrm{J}$ ✓)

questions.question: A cylinder is divided into two chambers by a piston. Left chamber: gas at $P_L$ and volume $V_L$. Right chamber: gas at $P_R$ and volume $V_R$. The piston is released. At equilibrium (same temperature $T$), it stops where $P_L' = P_R'$. If the total volume is $V_L + V_R$ and total moles are conserved, find $P_L' = P_R'$.
questions.answer:
At temperature $T$, total moles: $n = n_L + n_R = \dfrac{P_L V_L + P_R V_R}{RT}$

At equilibrium: $P_L' = P_R' = P_f$ (otherwise piston would still move), and total volume conserved:

$n = \dfrac{P_f(V_L + V_R)}{RT}$

Equating: $P_f = \dfrac{P_L V_L + P_R V_R}{V_L + V_R}$

This is the same as connecting two containers at the same temperature — the equilibrium pressure is the volume-weighted average.

questions.question: A vertical cylinder (cross-section $A = 50\ \mathrm{cm^2}$) is closed at the bottom and has a light frictionless piston. Gas of length $L_0 = 40\ \mathrm{cm}$ is trapped below at $T_0 = 27^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Atmospheric pressure $P_0 = 1.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$, $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, piston mass negligible. The gas is heated until the piston rises by $\Delta L = 10\ \mathrm{cm}$. Find the new temperature.
questions.answer:
Piston is massless and frictionless $\Rightarrow$ isobaric process at $P = P_0$.

$V_1 = A L_0 = 50\times10^{-4} \times 0.4 = 2\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m^3}$

$V_2 = A(L_0 + \Delta L) = 50\times10^{-4} \times 0.5 = 2.5\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m^3}$

Isobaric: $T_2/T_1 = V_2/V_1$

$T_2 = T_1 \times \dfrac{V_2}{V_1} = 300 \times \dfrac{2.5}{2.0} = 375\ \mathrm{K} = 102^\circ\mathrm{C}$

questions.question: A horizontal cylinder is divided by a piston (mass $m$, area $A$). The left side has gas at $P_1$ and the right side is at vacuum. The piston is released from rest. Describe the subsequent motion and the final equilibrium state (assuming the piston can be stopped by a wall at the right end).
questions.answer:
The left gas pushes the piston to the right with net force $F = P_1 A$ (no resistance from vacuum).

The piston accelerates to the right, compressing nothing on the right side.

The gas does work on the piston: $W = P_1 A \cdot \Delta x$ (but $P$ decreases as gas expands).

**If there's a wall at the right end** (say, the cylinder ends):

The piston hits the wall — energy is dissipated (inelastic collision). Eventually the piston comes to rest with gas filling the full cylinder volume $V_{\text{total}}$ and pressure:

$P_f = \dfrac{P_1 V_1}{V_{\text{total}}}$ (if isothermal)

The temperature may change depending on heat exchange. In the final equilibrium, $\Delta U = W_{\text{net}}$ plus heat from walls.
